analysis:
This batch has only test files (reslice floor wiring, scenario fixture, pure sizing tests, a Nemotron Super capacity test update) and one new shell script, scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh. The production re-slice change itself (EngineV2KVSizing.resliceGrants with minimumGrantBytes, the floors-first allocation) is not in the supplied units, so I could not review it. The tests assert that the sum of grants stays at or below the budget, that an infeasible floor total is still refused, and that the refusal leaves residents' grants unchanged. Those are availability and memory-safety properties relevant to T-029 and T-041 (KV grant and carve) and TB-007. I found no test-side regression.

The script scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh runs the app's own CLI with an empty environment (env -i, a fixed PATH, HOME under the new output folder, DARKBLOOM_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1). It uses set -euo pipefail, quotes its variables, and mkdir fails if the folder already exists. The app path and CLI name come from the caller (CI or release tooling), so it is not an attacker surface in the supplied evidence. It also invokes provider-cluster-runtime-models.py, which fetches the public catalog and CDN for the given environment. That Python script and the `cluster runtime-facts` CLI subcommand are not supplied, so I could not check them. The facts feed the cluster-runtime approval and qualification contract, which is a release and qualification path touching A-017 and T-054. Its integrity depends on trusted CI inputs, the catalog and CDN contents, and the unseen Python script and CLI, so those are open questions for the next pass. The script's output is derived data and is not validated here.

The fixture hard-codes model sizes and grants for tests only and handles no secrets or consumer data.
